summary:
The code claims hold against the tree. Get-CheckerControls plants both controls at WindowCases.ps1:6215, before scanStart at :6218, so the in-tree keep-folder tripwire is real. Get-HeaderCount matches the header as a prefix. Get-OracleRow sends code 1920 to other-code, so the correction to SC-136 is right. Fitness walks .taad/ (it is not in SKIP_DIRS). record.py deletes nothing, so a committed record would survive the engine's export. Two design-level problems remain, both major:
1. The hand-off sends the person to the SL-107 worktree and to the slice/SL-107 branch. Nothing in the slice waits for the person's run, though, so the slice will merge first, and a record committed to slice/SL-107 after that never reaches uat. The main checkout is on uat and has nothing built yet.
2. The criterion-5 reconciliation sets no hard floor. Its largest item, the layer-store rows, has only a lower bound, and the scans' 682 path lists are gone. So any shortfall, including a scanner under-count, can be put down to "Layers, rest unmeasured". Same-session anchor runs would give a real floor.
Smaller points:
- The counts-only rule is weaker than the writer it backs.
- The rule is never run against any file.
- The 0.5 GB vs 3 GB disagreement is marked resynthesis-forcing, when the brief already makes this the owner's run.

findings.claim: The hand-off pins the run and the commit to the SL-107 worktree and slice/SL-107. The design also says no machine-checked case waits on the person's run, so the slice reaches merge before the owner runs anything (Q-261 was decided while the owner was away). After the merge, slice/SL-107 is a dead branch, and a record committed there never reaches uat, which is where SC-136/SC-138 would look. The design also misreads $Repo. $Repo makes the record land in whichever checkout runs the script; it does not require the SL-107 worktree. The checkout the person will actually have is the main one, which is on uat (.git/HEAD: ref: refs/heads/uat) and has no artifacts/ build (Glob artifacts/*/*.{exe,dll} found nothing there). In that checkout the teed command `... | Tee-Object -FilePath artifacts\c-drive-console.txt` opens its file before Update-App has created artifacts\. File-writing cmdlets do not create missing parent folders (PowerShell issue #3363, Add-Content: 'Could not find a part of the path'). So the console capture either fails at once or is silently missing, and the capture is the only place a LEAK path survives. The cmdlet behaviour was not run here; settle it by running the teed command in a checkout with no artifacts\ folder.
findings.evidence: Design, contract 'W-001 whole-drive invocation' notes: '$Repo is the checkout the script runs from, so it has to be run in the SL-107 worktree.' Component 'The record': 'it is committed on slice/SL-107'. Key decision 2: 'Nothing in this slice's machine-checked cases waits on the person's run.' C:\Users\sshub\projets\filesystem-analyser-v2\.git\HEAD = ref: refs/heads/uat.
findings.fix: In SL-107-c-drive-run.md, name the place as 'a checkout of the branch that carries SL-107's merge (the main checkout on uat once SL-107 has merged; the SL-107 worktree only while it still exists)', and say to commit the record on that branch. Add `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force artifacts | Out-Null` before the teed command.

findings.claim:
The must-verify precondition 'every reconciling item has its own measurement or a stated bound' fails, and the design drops the one floor it could have.
- Item (a), the layer-store rows inside the old 682, is bounded only below ('at least 25 … the rest is unmeasured').
- Item (f), fixture churn, is a guessed ±12, although it is measurable.
- The result is stated as 'no hard floor'.

The data that would bound (a) is gone. A Glob of %TEMP%\taad3-runs for a-c-drive.json, failed-folders-C.csv, C.rows.tsv, open-refused.tsv and misses.tsv found none. The record is counts-only, and the hook log is deleted. So Q-261's condition, 'names the cause of every difference from 682 by path group', can be met only by putting whatever is left over down to 'Containers\Layers'.

That makes criterion 5 one-sided. Criteria 2-4 compare the panel with the engine's own list, so they cannot see an engine that fails to record a folder at all (the U-109 shape). Criterion 5 is the only whole-drive check against that, and as designed it absorbs any shortfall. Read strictly instead, Q-261 would turn a correct run's unnameable gap into a false 'finding about the scanner'. The same gap catches lesson #360: new code-363 leftovers from later cloud cases push 363 past 27-28. Q-261 then files that as a scanner finding, and nothing in the run tells it apart from fixture growth.
findings.evidence: Design key decision 3: 'Result: code 5 at most about 627 …; rows at most about 660; no hard floor.' The cross_domain_transfer invariant 'Every reconciling item has its own measurement or a stated bound' is must-verify. Glob of C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp\taad3-runs for the five spike path-list files found none. The record writer emits counts only:

quote.text: # Writes W-001's record as JSON: integers, booleans, fixed names, the commit, and reasons from the panel's own table.

findings.fix: Replace 'no hard floor' with a floor measured in the same session. Right after the C:\ run, while the caches are warm (lesson #403: about 0 added pool when warm), the person runs the existing W-001 over three disjoint bounded roots: C:\Windows, C:\ProgramData and C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp. The C:\ rows must be at least their sum, less churn. The remainder is named as 'rows outside these three', and the Temp anchor gives that day's fixture count (363, the fsa-window-cases leftovers). The doc should also say plainly that the old Layers share cannot be measured because the path lists are gone. This needs no code change; the person records the anchor counts beside the record.

findings.claim: The counts-only rule is weaker than the writer it is meant to back. Write-W001Record refuses any string that contains a backslash or a slash, but the rule fires only on a drive letter followed by an escaped backslash or a slash, or on a "path" key. A UNC path (\\\\srv\\share), a relative path (Users\\sshub\\…) or a %VAR%-rooted path would get through a hand edit. The invariant can be enforced as it stands rather than remembered. In ConvertTo-Json output, a backslash pair only appears where a string contains a backslash, and a slash is never escaped, so the writer's own test can be expressed exactly over the file text.
findings.evidence: Writer predicate at WindowCases.ps1:6182 (`$value -match '[\\/]'` refuses). The rule at .taad/fitness.yaml:1297 is narrower.
findings.fix: Replace the first pattern with '\\\\|/' (an escaped backslash pair or any slash in the JSON text). This mirrors the writer's [\\/] on the decoded strings and does not fire on the \" escape.
findings.class_of: path spellings without a drive letter

findings.claim: The new rule is never run against any file. Its file does not exist until the person commits it, and Fitness treats a rule that matches no file as a pass (Q-012). The design's only case for it says 'Not run as a case'. Nothing shows that the rule stays quiet on a real record or fires on a path-bearing one (CC-007).
findings.evidence: Design case 'commit the person's record / the committed file contains a path': 'Not run as a case: the file exists only after the person's run.'
findings.fix: Add one validate check in a scratch copy. Place a real record, the gitignored artifacts\w001-run.json from a bounded W-001 run, at .taad/slices/SL-089/c-drive-run.json and run Fitness op=check: expect quiet. Then add a string with a drive path and one with a UNC path: expect the rule to fire.

findings.claim:
The decidable disagreement over the 0.5 GB and 3 GB pool guards is marked would_force_resynthesis: true. It cannot change the design.
- The brief names the run the owner's ('Owner runs W-001…').
- Lesson #348 predicts a cold full exe scan at 3-4.4 GiB, so even a 3 GB guard would not make this an engine run.
Leaving it marked as forcing a resynthesis invites a design lap that can only arrive back here.
findings.evidence: Design decidable_disagreements[0]: 'If the 3 GB guard applies to validate … Criteria 1-5 would then move from a person's run to a machine check of the record', would_force_resynthesis: true. Lesson #348: 'a cold exe-full is predicted at 3-4.4 GiB'.
findings.fix: Set would_force_resynthesis to false, and record that the slice is the owner's run whichever guard figure applies.

dimensions_checked.result: M2: the reconciliation's bounded-item precondition fails. Item (a) has only a lower bound, the old path lists are gone (my Glob found none), and the design says 'no hard floor'. The recalled claims I checked hold: Fitness walks .taad/ (fitness.py:348-350 SKIP_DIRS has no .taad; os.walk at :430), and record.py has no unlink or rmtree, so a committed record survives the export.

Within M1: Tee-Object in a checkout with no artifacts\ folder. Within M2: fixture growth from later cloud cases (lesson #360) pushing 363 out of 27-28. Checked and found fine: an elevated shell (Inconclusive), `-Root C:`, a stopped run's Cancelled record (the doc says do not commit it), and the store as a notScanned line next to the header's prefix match.
m1: the counts-only rule is narrower than the writer's own [\\/] refusal, so it relies on remembering rather than holding by construction.

None. No code change, wrapper or judging script. The appended settled rule costs about 30 s of harness and RuleCases at validate (Q-027, lesson #212), and its settled count is derived, not pinned (SettledCountProbe 'ExpectedSettled: derived count').
M1: the run location and commit branch assume the SL-107 worktree outlives a merge that the design itself lets happen first. The main checkout is on uat with no build.

Checked Test-W001 at 6202-6303. A missing report returns before any record is written (6226). A failed check still writes a record with verdict failed (6260, 6294). A stray string throws, and nothing is written (6188). Pool is only read and recorded (6217, 6221, 6290), never guarded. The endings table covers these. A commit string emptied by a git failure would throw at write after a full scan; git is present on this PC, so not filed.

m3: the guard disagreement is marked resynthesis-forcing against the brief's 'Owner runs'. The correction to SC-136 matches Get-OracleRow (6136-6137: 363 first, then any code other than 5 goes to other-code and so to notARefusedKeepShape at 6257). Q-261 is honoured in form, but see M2 on its 'every difference named'.

Q-114 is not triggered, because WindowCases.ps1 is unchanged. CC-002 does not apply: fitness.yaml:15-17 defines settled entries as having no twin. CC-004: the cmd.exe case uses a temporary .cmd file rather than a committed command; this is low value because the survey already measured it, so not filed. CC-009 does not apply, since no new scratch-creating driver is added.

m2: the new rule is never exercised. The other cases are runnable unattended: the doc-text Select-String checks, the W-001 runs on D:\, ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows and fsa-guard-tests, and the W001Oracle corpus F02 and F12. The in-run tripwire holds: controls are planted at 6215, before scanStart at 6218, and the deny ACL is set at 6156, so ChangeUtc cannot exempt the keep folder.

Paths stay out of git. The writer refuses them (6182, 6188), artifacts/ is gitignored (.gitignore:7), and LEAK lines go only to the console and its capture. m1 notes that the backing rule misses path spellings with no drive letter.
